title: Transfer of adjunctions from étale to pro-étale finite coefficients
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p
e\ell$. Let $X,Y$ be separated schemes of finite type over $k$, and let $f:X	o Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-morphism, in the standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$ (a finite admissible ring). On the small étale and pro-étale sites use the constant-$A$ module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $\Dctf$ for the full subcategories of bounded complexes with constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude: there is a finite interval containing the cohomology of the derived tensor with every degree-zero module sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, sk-def-sfb-constructible].
Write $
u_T^*$ for the derived comparison functors [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], assumed to restrict to equivalences
$
u_T^*:\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{ét}},A)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Dctf(T,A)$ for $T=X,Y$. Choose quasi-inverses $Q_T$ and their equivalence isomorphisms. Let $Rf_!$ be the functor of [sk-prop-sf-existence], and let $Rf^{\mathrm{ét}}_!$ be the étale compact-support functor for the same chosen compactification [def-amb-etale-compact-support], restricted to $\Dctf$. Let
$c_f:
u_Y^*Rf^{\mathrm{ét}}_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_!
u_X^*$ be the compact-support comparison on $\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$. Suppose
$G:\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{ét}},A)	o\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ is a right adjoint of
$Rf^{\mathrm{ét}}_!$ with counit $\varepsilon^{\mathrm{ét}}$. Then
$G^{\mathrm{pro}}=
u_X^*\circ G\circ Q_Y$ is right adjoint to
$Rf_!$ on $\Dctf(-_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$, with counit, under the equivalence identifications $Q_Y
u_Y^*N\simeq N$ and $G^{\mathrm{pro}}
u_Y^*N\simeq
u_X^*GN$,
$$\varepsilon^{\mathrm{pro}}_{
u_Y^*N}=
u_Y^*(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{ét}}_N)\circ c_f(GN)^{-1}.$$
The unique counit-preserving isomorphism identifies $G^{\mathrm{pro}}$ with the restriction to $\Dctf$ of the Brown adjoint $f^!$ of [sk-prop-sf-existence] on the localizing closures [sk-def-localizing-closure].

proof.text: Compose the supplied etale adjunction with eY.toAdjunction. Compose on the source with eX.symm.toAdjunction and transport the left functor along the natural isomorphism built from cf and eX.counitIso. Mathlib Adjunction.comp and ofNatIsoLeft construct the requested pro-etale adjunction. No additional full-faithfulness theorem is needed because the equivalences are explicit hypotheses.

Expand ofNatIsoLeft_counit and comp_counit_app. Naturality of cf.inv and the inverse triangle identity of eX cancel the source-equivalence factors. At eY(N), counit_app_functor, naturality of the etale counit and naturality of cf.inv give exactly the displayed formula.

Identify the finite-value bounded constructibility predicate with the source finite-stalk predicate using lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison and the equivalence between interval vanishing and t-boundedness. Mapping this equivalence through comparisonUpperStar identifies proEtaleProperty with the source constructibleFiniteTor. Its shift lemma proves shift stability of the generators. The Tor predicates coincide definitionally.

Given the Brown adjunction on localizing closures, transpose the counit of the already transported adjunction to a map alpha from its generator-valued right adjoint into the Brown right-adjoint value. On Hom from each shifted generator, naturality identifies composition with alpha with the composite of the two adjunction Hom bijections and the fully faithful inclusion Hom bijections. This is bijective. Complete alpha to a distinguished triangle. Its cone lies in the localizing closure, and Hom exactness, together with surjectivity in the original degree and injectivity after shifting, makes all maps from shifted generators to the cone zero. To see that such a cone is zero, put B equal to the right orthogonal of the shift closure of the generators and R equal to the left orthogonal of B. Mathlib orthogonal instances show R triangulated and replete; colimit.hom_ext proves closure under all existing coproducts. R contains the generators, hence the cone. The cone is also in B, so its identity is zero. Thus alpha is an isomorphism, and repleteness gives hJ. This replaces the separate geometric preservation theorem with a direct argument from the two supplied adjunctions.

The two toLocalizing inclusions are fully faithful ιOfLE functors. The lower-shriek and right-adjoint squares commute definitionally. Apply Adjunction.restrictFullyFaithful. Its map_restrictFullyFaithful_counit_app identifies the restricted counit with exactly the Brown ambient counit.

Apply rightAdjointUniq to the transported adjunction and the restricted Brown adjunction. Its hom_app_counit equation, mapped through the full inclusion, is the desired ambient equation. Conversely injectivity of the inverse restricted Brown Hom equivalence forces any counit-compatible isomorphism to equal this one, componentwise.

proof_origin.place: Both proof paragraphs: adjunction transfer, counit and Brown identification. Brown generator preservation is proved directly by comparing the two supplied adjunctions and detecting the comparison on shifted generators; Mathlib triangulated orthogonals and Hom exactness supply the categorical tools.

lean.note: Uses the ordinary constant-ring module-sheaf presentation, canonically equivalent to both the continuous-function coefficient module category and the finite-discrete internal module-object category. The exact finite-value etale constructibility predicate is used, not the different generic finitely-generated-stalk predicate. The comparison forward functors are constrained to the recorded termwise inverse images, and cf is constrained to the canonical proper-mate/open-extension compact-support comparison for the same chosen compactification. The Brown clause quantifies over its adjunction on the recorded localizing closure in this ordinary coefficient presentation, concludes finite-Tor constructible preservation, and gives the unique ambient counit-compatible natural isomorphism. No statement correction or missing mathematical notion.
